best_for: Kids aged 10-15 who love logical thinking
Students who want to move beyond block coding
not_for: Very young kids (under 8) who cannot read well
target_audience.who_should_take_foundation_first: Beginners can start here, but completing Scratch Programming first is helpful.

prerequisites.recommended: Familiarity with visual block coding (like Scratch).

system_requirements.hardware: A computer (Windows or Mac) with at least 4GB RAM.

overview.positioning: A bridge from visual coding to professional text-based programming for kids.
overview.short_description: Level up your coding skills! Transition from Scratch to real-world languages like Python and HTML/CSS using professional tools like VS Code.

key_facts.capstone: A Multi-Page Website or Python Text Adventure Game

what_you_will_be_able_to_do: Translate block logic into text-based Python code
Write functional Python scripts with variables and loops
Design and code a multi-page HTML/CSS website
Use VS Code just like professional programmers do

why_now.industry_shift: Coding is becoming a universal language.
why_now.ai_impact: Understanding code helps kids understand how AI systems are built.
why_now.business_demand: Analytical and computational thinking are highly valued skills.
why_now.career_opportunity: Sets a strong foundation for high school computer science.

learning_outcomes: TRANSITION: Move confidently from Scratch blocks to Python text.
PROGRAM: Write Python scripts that solve math puzzles or play games.
BUILD: Construct web pages using raw HTML and CSS code.
OPERATE: Navigate and use an industry-standard IDE (VS Code).

stages.focus: Building websites from scratch using HTML/CSS.
Using VS Code to manage projects.

core_tools.what_student_learns: Syntax, data types, loops, and functions
File management, syntax highlighting, and debugging
Complex logic before translating to text

industry_workflow.overview: The software development lifecycle adapted for young minds.

stages.name: Design
stages.desc: Planning what the code should do.

stages.name: Write
stages.desc: Typing the code in VS Code.

stages.name: Run
stages.desc: Executing the program to see if it works.

stages.name: Debug
stages.desc: Fixing the spelling mistakes and logic errors.

ai_integration.ai_can_assist_with: Explaining complex error messages in VS Code.
ai_integration.ai_cannot_replace: The student's fundamental understanding of logic.
ai_integration.human_expertise_required: Instructors guide students through syntax errors.
ai_integration.responsible_use: Encouraging typing code manually rather than generating it.

best_practices: Always use descriptive variable names (e.g., 'player_score' instead of 'x').
Save files with the correct extensions (.py, .html, .css).
Read the error messages carefully; they usually tell you exactly what went wrong.

common_mistakes.why_it_happens: Transitioning from blocks where syntax isn't an issue.
common_mistakes.professional_approach: Pay close attention to syntax rules and let VS Code formatting guide you.

common_mistakes.mistake: Mixing up HTML tags and CSS properties.
common_mistakes.professional_approach: Keep HTML (structure) and CSS (style) in separate files to avoid confusion.

career_paths.employer_expectations: Strong grasp of fundamental programming concepts.
career_paths.what_student_demonstrates: Ability to write text-based code from scratch.

freelance_applications.portfolio_requirements: GitHub repository (optional) or folder of functioning scripts and web pages.

what_you_will_build: A multi-page website about a favorite topic
A final customized project combining learned skills
final_deliverables: A working Python application with user inputs and logic
A fully styled, multi-page HTML/CSS website

assessment.criteria: Code runs without errors, meets project requirements, uses proper syntax.

certification.title: Young Coder Professional Certificate
certification.criteria: Successfully complete and submit the final Python and Web projects.

next_learning_path.recommended_next: Python for Kids or Web Design for Kids

faq.question: Is typing required?
faq.answer: Yes, this course transitions to text-based coding, so basic typing skills are highly recommended.

faq.question: Do we need to install software?
faq.answer: Yes, we will guide you through installing Python and VS Code, which are free, professional tools.

faq.question: Is this too hard for a 10-year-old?
faq.answer: If they have a strong interest in computers and enjoy logical puzzles, they will do great! We break everything down step-by-step.

modules.module_title: From Blocks to Text: Introduction to Python
modules.module_purpose: Bridge the gap between visual coding and text-based programming.
what_you_will_learn: Using the print() and input() functions

lessons.what_is_taught: The print function and basic strings.
lessons.why_it_matters: It's the first step to making the computer talk to you in text.
lessons.what_learner_does: Writes their first 'Hello World' and prints a custom message.
lessons.expected_outcome: A script that outputs text to the console.

lessons.why_it_matters: Variables are the memory of your program.
lessons.what_learner_does: Creates variables for a character's name, age, and power level.
lessons.expected_outcome: A script that prints dynamic sentences using variables.

lessons.what_learner_does: Builds a 'Mad Libs' style story generator.
lessons.expected_outcome: An interactive story that changes based on user input.

modules.hands_on_practice: Write a script that asks for user details and performs a calculation.
modules.assignment: Submit the Mad Libs generator script.
modules.expected_outcome: Comfortable with basic Python syntax and I/O.

modules.module_title: Python Logic: Making Decisions and Looping
modules.module_purpose: Teach the program how to make choices and repeat tasks efficiently.

lessons.why_it_matters: Allows the program to react differently based on conditions.
lessons.expected_outcome: A script with basic branching logic.

lessons.what_is_taught: Multiple conditions and logical operators (and, or).
lessons.what_learner_does: Builds a grade calculator (A, B, C, etc.).
lessons.expected_outcome: A script with complex conditional logic.

lessons.what_is_taught: While loops and avoiding infinite loops.
lessons.why_it_matters: Keeps a game running until the user quits.
lessons.what_learner_does: Builds a simple number guessing game.

lessons.what_is_taught: For loops and the range() function.
lessons.why_it_matters: Great for counting and repeating a specific number of times.
lessons.what_learner_does: Creates a countdown timer and a multiplication table generator.

modules.hands_on_practice: Combine loops and conditionals to build a Rock-Paper-Scissors game.
modules.assignment: Submit the completed Rock-Paper-Scissors Python script.
modules.expected_outcome: Ability to write programs with complex logic and loops.

modules.module_title: Setting Up Shop: VS Code and HTML Basics
modules.module_purpose: Introduce professional developer tools and the foundation of web pages.

lessons.what_is_taught: Installing VS Code, creating folders, and making files.
lessons.why_it_matters: This is the actual tool professional developers use.
lessons.what_learner_does: Sets up a project workspace and creates their first .html file.

lessons.why_it_matters: Every web page needs this structure to work properly.
lessons.what_learner_does: Writes a valid HTML5 boilerplate document.
lessons.expected_outcome: A blank but valid web page.

lessons.what_learner_does: Builds an informational page about their favorite animal.

lessons.why_it_matters: Connects pages together and adds visual appeal.
lessons.what_learner_does: Adds photos and links to a second HTML page.

modules.hands_on_practice: Build a two-page interlinked website with text and images.
modules.assignment: Submit the HTML files for the two-page site.
modules.expected_outcome: Comfortable using an IDE and writing raw HTML.

modules.module_title: Styling the Web: Introduction to CSS
modules.module_purpose: Learn how to make plain HTML websites look professional and colorful.

lessons.why_it_matters: Separating style from structure makes coding easier.
lessons.what_learner_does: Creates a style.css file and links it to their HTML.

lessons.why_it_matters: Allows you to style specific parts of a page differently.
lessons.what_learner_does: Styles specific paragraphs and headings using classes.

lessons.what_is_taught: Hex codes, RGB, font-family, and text alignment.
lessons.why_it_matters: Defines the visual theme of the website.
lessons.what_learner_does: Applies a cohesive color scheme and custom fonts.

lessons.why_it_matters: Controls spacing and layout of elements.
lessons.what_learner_does: Creates styled buttons and spaced-out sections.
lessons.expected_outcome: A neatly laid out and formatted web page.

modules.hands_on_practice: Apply a full CSS stylesheet to the two-page website built in Module 3.
modules.assignment: Submit the complete, styled multi-page website project.
modules.expected_outcome: Ability to independently style HTML structures using CSS.
